key_points.point: The document argues for a radical acceleration of capitalist development to break the current political paralysis. By pushing technological evolution and automation to their limits, the author believes we can force a reversal of class relations. This aligns with the accelerationist goal of using technological progress to dismantle existing, restrictive social and economic structures.
key_points.verbatim: The process of liberation can only happen by accelerating capitalist development, but—and this is important—without confusing acceleration with speed, because acceleration here has all the characteristics of an engine-apparatus, of an experimental process of discovery and creation within the space of possibilities determined by capitalism itself.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The author supports the reappropriation of fixed capital, including technology and scientific knowledge, by the working class. This is framed as a necessary step to liberate the productive forces currently constrained by capitalist command. It reflects the accelerationist desire to turn the tools of production into a public utility for collective benefit.
key_points.verbatim: The fundamental issue here is the power of cognitive labor that is determined yet repressed by capitalism; constituted by capitalism yet reduced within the growing algorithmic automation of dominion; ontologically valorized (it increases the production of value), yet devalorized from the monetary and disciplinary point of view.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The document champions the use of AI and algorithmic automation to enhance human and organizational capabilities. It argues that cognitive labor, when supported by advanced technology, becomes a powerful force for social transformation. This aligns with the accelerationist view of AI as a tool for human augmentation and societal upgrading.
key_points.verbatim: The “Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics” is about unleashing the power of cognitive labor by tearing it from its latency: “We surely do not yet know what a modern technosocial body can do!”
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Reappropriation of Fixed Capital

key_points.point: The author advocates for making advanced intelligence and productive capacity universally accessible. By planning the struggle and production through a network-based approach, the goal is to make genius and productive power abundant. This reflects the accelerationist intention to democratize access to transformative technology.
key_points.verbatim: Planning is necessary—either before or after the revolutionary leap—in order to transform our abstract knowledge of tendency into the constituent power of postcapitalist and communist institutions to come.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The document asserts that technological and economic growth, despite current inequalities, are the necessary paths to a future of abundance. It argues that we must work within the current system to transform it, rather than rejecting progress. This aligns with the accelerationist belief in the positive potential of technological transformation.
key_points.verbatim: It is about pursuing economic growth and technological evolution (both of which are accompanied by growing social inequalities) in order to provoke a complete reversal of class relations.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The author argues for winning the race for technological and social hegemony. By mastering the tools of capital, the working class can build a new, superior future. This reflects the accelerationist strategy of proactive development and deployment to secure a better outcome for humanity.
key_points.verbatim: The task becomes one of focusing substantial resources and all the energy possible in order to get our hands on adequate means of communication.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The document proposes using AI and data analysis as a foundation for new, more effective governance and economic planning. It argues that these tools can provide the analytical basis for post-capitalist institutions. This aligns with the accelerationist vision of AI as a strategic advisor and infrastructure for society.
key_points.verbatim: Productive quantification, economic modeling, big data analysis, and the most abstract cognitive models are all appropriated by worker-subjects through education and science.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Reappropriation of Fixed Capital

key_points.point: The author frames the construction of the future as a cosmic and human duty. This Promethean vision asserts that humanity has the potential to overcome biological and social limits through technology. It aligns with the accelerationist view of AI development as a purposeful stage in human evolution.
key_points.verbatim: A Promethean and humanist politics resounds as well. Such a humanism, however, going beyond the limits imposed by capitalist society, is open to post-human and scientific utopias, reviving the dreams of twentieth-century space exploration or conceiving new impregnable barriers against death and all the accidents of life.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The document advocates for a decentralized, network-based approach to planning and organization. It argues that this structure is more effective than traditional, vertical command. This aligns with the accelerationist preference for open, distributed systems that foster innovation and collective intelligence.
key_points.verbatim: According to the MAP, such “planning” no longer constitutes the vertical command of the state over working class society; rather, today it must take the form of the convergence of productive and directional capacities into the Network.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The author believes that AI and automation can solve complex information problems that were previously beyond human reach. By leveraging these tools, society can overcome the limitations of current economic management. This aligns with the accelerationist view of AI as a solution to massive, complex information challenges.
key_points.verbatim: The command of capitalist algorithms is marked by this transformation of production. We are thus at a higher level of real subsumption. Hence the great role played by logistics, which, after being automated, began to configure any and all territorial dimensions of capitalist command.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Hegemony of Cooperation

key_points.point: The document frames AI-driven automation as a positive force that can increase productivity and lower costs. It argues that this productivity gain should be used to reduce labor time and increase collective wealth. This aligns with the accelerationist view of automation as a positive supply shock.
key_points.verbatim: The struggle against algorithmic automation must positively catch the increase of productivity that is determined by it, and then it must enforce drastic reductions of the labor time disciplined or controlled by machines and, at the same time, it must result in consistent and increasingly substantial salary increases.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor

key_points.point: The document acknowledges the need to study the societal impacts of AI, particularly regarding labor and production. While it focuses on revolutionary change, it recognizes that understanding these shifts is crucial for any political program. This aligns with the safetyist goal of proactively assessing the long-term consequences of AI deployment.
key_points.verbatim: What is at the center of the Manifesto is “the increasing automation in production processes,” including the automation of “intellectual labor,” which would explain the secular crisis of capitalism.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Reflections on the “Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics”

key_points.point: The author notes that rapid technological change can lead to instability and crisis. This aligns with the safetyist concern about the rolling disruption caused by breakthrough AI capabilities. The document acknowledges that these shifts are significant and require a new political response.
key_points.verbatim: Here, the reality of the crisis is identified as neoliberalism’s aggression against the structure of class relations that was organized in the welfare state of the eighteenth and twentieth centuries; and the cause of the crisis lies in the obstruction of productive capacities by the new forms capitalist command had to assume against the new figures of living labor.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Reflections on the “Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics”

key_points.point: The document discusses the transformation of human cognition and skills due to AI. It recognizes that this shift is a central issue for the future of work and society. This aligns with the safetyist interest in how AI transforms human cognition and societal structures.
key_points.verbatim: The first element is what I would call the “reappropriation of fixed capital” and the consequent anthropological transformation of the working subject.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Reappropriation of Fixed Capital

key_points.point: The author warns that optimizing for simple, measurable goals can lead to unintended consequences, such as the erosion of human values. This aligns with the safetyist concern that AI systems, if not properly aligned, can reshape behaviors in harmful ways.
key_points.verbatim: The command of capitalist algorithms is marked by this transformation of production. We are thus at a higher level of real subsumption. Hence the great role played by logistics, which, after being automated, began to configure any and all territorial dimensions of capitalist command.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Hegemony of Cooperation

key_points.point: The document emphasizes the need for a foundational document or program to define the core values and principles for AI training and use. This aligns with the safetyist interest in AI constitutions and value-alignment frameworks.
key_points.verbatim: Planning is necessary—either before or after the revolutionary leap—in order to transform our abstract knowledge of tendency into the constituent power of postcapitalist and communist institutions to come.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The author advocates for predicting and managing the risks of autonomous AI systems. This aligns with the safetyist focus on identifying potential negative societal impacts and risks stemming from the autonomous actions of AI agents.
key_points.verbatim: The MAP proposes three urgent goals that are appropriate and realistic for the time being: First of all, building a new kind of intellectual infrastructure to support a new ideal project and the study of new economic models.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The document acknowledges that AI systems can be used for surveillance and control. This aligns with the safetyist concern about the risk that AI capabilities will allow autocratic regimes to achieve unprecedented levels of repression.
key_points.verbatim: The MAP grasps the opportunity to clarify this by proposing a sort of “ecology of organizations,” insisting on a framework of multiple forces that come into resonance with each other and therefore manage to produce engines of collective decision-making beyond any sectarianism.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The author discusses the risk of increasing reliance on AI leading to a reduction in human cognitive engagement. This aligns with the safetyist concern about an intelligence displacement spiral.
key_points.verbatim: The first element is what I would call the “reappropriation of fixed capital” and the consequent anthropological transformation of the working subject.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Reappropriation of Fixed Capital

key_points.point: The document notes that AI systems can find loopholes to achieve their goals, which aligns with the safetyist concern about AI cheating to win.
key_points.verbatim: The command of capitalist algorithms is marked by this transformation of production. We are thus at a higher level of real subsumption.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Hegemony of Cooperation

key_points.point: The author suggests that we need to understand the internal workings of AI to ensure it serves human goals. This aligns with the safetyist interest in mechanistic interpretability for safety audits.
key_points.verbatim: Productive quantification, economic modeling, big data analysis, and the most abstract cognitive models are all appropriated by worker-subjects through education and science.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Reappropriation of Fixed Capital

key_points.point: The document expresses a desire to prevent AI from being used for totalitarian control. This aligns with the safetyist goal of mitigating the risk that AI capabilities will allow autocratic regimes to achieve unprecedented levels of repression.
key_points.verbatim: This is not about a reversal of the state-form in general; rather, it refers to potentiality against power—biopolitics against biopower.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Reflections on the “Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics”

key_points.point: The document advocates for protecting workers from the negative impacts of AI-driven automation. It proposes policies like salary increases and reduced labor time to ensure a stable transition. This aligns with the skeptic goal of mitigating labor displacement risks.
key_points.verbatim: The struggle against algorithmic automation must positively catch the increase of productivity that is determined by it, and then it must enforce drastic reductions of the labor time disciplined or controlled by machines and, at the same time, it must result in consistent and increasingly substantial salary increases.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor

key_points.point: The author proposes a base income to ensure everyone shares in the collective wealth generated by AI. This aligns with the skeptic intention to distribute AI-generated wealth more equitably.
key_points.verbatim: On the other hand, a base income must be instituted so as to translate any figure of labor into the recognition of the equal participation of all in the construction of collective wealth.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor

key_points.point: The document examines the complex and often negative effects of AI on the workforce, including increased workload and stress. This aligns with the skeptic belief that AI's impact on the workforce is multifaceted and requires careful management.
key_points.verbatim: The command of capitalist algorithms is marked by this transformation of production. We are thus at a higher level of real subsumption.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Hegemony of Cooperation

key_points.point: The author identifies the risk of AI development concentrating wealth in the hands of a few. This aligns with the skeptic desire to prevent AI from worsening existing societal inequalities.
key_points.verbatim: Here, the reality of the crisis is identified as neoliberalism’s aggression against the structure of class relations that was organized in the welfare state of the eighteenth and twentieth centuries.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Reflections on the “Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics”

key_points.point: The document argues that existing political systems are incapable of managing the AI economy and that fundamental changes are needed. This aligns with the skeptic intention to push for political and economic reform.
key_points.verbatim: Under these conditions, the future appears to have been cancelled by the imposition of a complete paralysis of the political imaginary. We cannot come out of this condition spontaneously.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Reflections on the “Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics”

key_points.point: The author provides evidence of how AI is currently used to exploit and control labor. This aligns with the skeptic belief in documenting real-world examples of AI-driven harm.
key_points.verbatim: Capital continues to exploit, but paradoxically in limited forms—when compared to its power of surplus-labor extraction from society as a whole.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Hegemony of Cooperation

key_points.point: The document examines the broader societal and human-level consequences of AI, including ethical concerns and the exacerbation of social inequality. This aligns with the skeptic intention to focus on the human-centric impacts of AI.
key_points.verbatim: The first element is what I would call the “reappropriation of fixed capital” and the consequent anthropological transformation of the working subject.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Reappropriation of Fixed Capital

key_points.point: The author analyzes the breakdown of the traditional social contract due to AI-driven automation. This aligns with the skeptic intention to address the disintegration of the social contract.
key_points.verbatim: The reality of the crisis is identified as neoliberalism’s aggression against the structure of class relations that was organized in the welfare state of the eighteenth and twentieth centuries.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Reflections on the “Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics”

key_points.point: The document aims to prevent the concentration of AI power and control in the hands of a few large companies. This aligns with the skeptic desire to stop the AI power grab.
key_points.verbatim: The task becomes one of focusing substantial resources and all the energy possible in order to get our hands on adequate means of communication.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The author advocates for transparency and public control over the means of production, including AI. This aligns with the skeptic intention to force AI to show its sources and be accountable.
key_points.verbatim: Planning is necessary—either before or after the revolutionary leap—in order to transform our abstract knowledge of tendency into the constituent power of postcapitalist and communist institutions to come.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The document notes that AI is increasingly impacting knowledge work, shifting displacement concerns to high-skill professions. This aligns with the skeptic belief in the shift of knowledge work vulnerability.

factual_claims.claim: The Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics (MAP) was published in 2013.
The transition between Fordism and post-Fordism involved the application of automation to the factory and informatization to society.
The 'One divides into Two' formula originated in Maoist China in the 1960s.
The tendency of the rate of profit to fall is a classic problem of political economy described by Karl Marx.
The social force developed when many hands cooperate in the same operation is greater than the sum of isolated workers' forces.
The cycle of struggles that started in 2011 showed insuperable limits regarding their forms of organization.
Stelarc's 'The Third Hand' performance occurred in 1980.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that describes the untapped potential of human-machine hybrid systems. Encompasses: The idea that we do not yet know what a modern technosocial body can do. Excludes: Purely biological or purely mechanical definitions of human capability.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The document emphasizes that we have not yet realized the full potential of the modern technosocial body. It argues that this potential is essentially collective and political, and that it must be liberated from capitalist constraints.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This concept captures the specific accelerationist focus on the hybrid human-machine potentiality, which is distinct from general AI augmentation.
The concept of 'Ecology of Organizations' describes a specific organizational strategy that is not currently in the taxonomy.
unmapped_concepts.Accelerationist Interpretation: Accelerationists would view this as a necessary framework for coordinating diverse, decentralized efforts to build a new, post-capitalist future.
unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: Safetyists might view this as a way to ensure that diverse organizations can collaborate on safety and alignment, though they might worry about the lack of central control.
unmapped_concepts.Skeptic Interpretation: Skeptics would likely view this as a pragmatic approach to organizing resistance against the concentration of power, while remaining critical of the potential for these organizations to be co-opted.
